n: A call to return: “Come, let us return to the LORD.” The God who wounded will heal; the one who struck will bandage. Discipline and healing come from the same loving hand.

f.w: let us return unto the LORD
he hath torn, and he will heal us

n: “After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up.” Originally a promise of quick national recovery, many Christians see in it a foreshadowing of Christ’s resurrection on the third day.

f.w: in the third day he will raise us up

n: Let us press on to know the Lord. His coming is as certain as sunrise, and He will come like spring rains that water the earth. Seeking God brings refreshment.

f.w: if we follow on to know the LORD

f.g: Autumn and spring rains that made crops grow in Israel.

n: God answers with heartbreak: “What shall I do with you?” Their devotion vanishes like morning mist or early dew—gone by mid-morning. Shallow repentance does not last.

f.w: your goodness is as a morning cloud

n: So God cut them down through the prophets and their words of judgment. His judgments shine out like light—clear and unmistakable.

f.w: I have slain them by the words of my mouth

n: One of the Old Testament’s great verses: God wants loyal love more than sacrifice, and knowing Him more than burnt offerings. Jesus quoted it twice to correct those who valued ritual over compassion.

f.w: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice

n: “Like Adam” (the Hebrew can read either “like men” or “like Adam”) they broke the covenant and betrayed God. Some read “at Adam,” a town by the Jordan.

f.w: they like men have transgressed the covenant
f.g: Or “like Adam” or “at Adam” (a town near the Jordan).

n: Gilead, east of the Jordan, is a city of evildoers stained with bloody footprints.

f.g: A region east of the Jordan; here possibly a city in it.

n: Gangs of priests lie in wait like robbers to murder travelers on the road to Shechem—a city of refuge and worship. Religious leaders have become criminals.

f.w: murder in the way by consent
f.g: Many translations read “murder on the way to Shechem.”

n: God has seen something horrible in Israel: Ephraim’s unfaithfulness has defiled the nation.
Judah too has a “harvest” of judgment appointed—yet the closing phrase hints at future restoration when God restores His people’s fortunes.

f.w: he hath set an harvest for thee
I returned the captivity of my people
f.g: When I restore the fortunes of My people.
